correctness.rationale: The analytic proof reconstructs the mixed-spectral divided-difference Jacobian, computes all three absolute coefficient row sums for both endpoint operators, factors the sharp 3/2 diagonal gap into a nonnegative polynomial, and shows the other endpoint norm is strictly below 3/2. Every nonsingular segment point has derivative norm strictly below 3/2; absolute continuity and the rank-one determinant-zero-line exception prove strict global inequality. Explicit rank-one spectral data give directional ratios tending to 3/2. The standalone check.py replay passed 2,711 assertions, including exact fractional Jacobians and an exact polynomial identity; finite checks are not substituted for universal proof.

originality.rationale: Higham gives the spectral positive-part rule, while Malick–Sendov and Šilhavý give broad derivative formulas. These are genuine prerequisites but the inspected statements do not evaluate the induced entrywise maximum norm at sharp value 3/2 or prove strict finite-pair nonattainment. The present argument performs a nontrivial rotation-dependent absolute-row-sum optimization and a global singular-line integration argument. Database similarity searches on PSD clipping, crossed norms, Jacobians and exact 3/2 returned neighboring projection results for different target sets/norms, not an implication of this theorem; this is not a guarantee of historical uniqueness.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not independently certified. An older Lorentz-cone or matrix positive-part entrywise perturbation result may be equivalent under a coordinate transformation.

value.rationale: Frobenius-positive-semidefinite repair is the standard local eigenvalue-clipping primitive in covariance denoising and semidefinite approximation, but errors may be bounded per entry rather than in Frobenius norm. The exact 50% worst-case amplification and its strict nonattainment quantify a natural stability mismatch. The smallest nonpolyhedral PSD cone is a motivated natural cutoff, not an arbitrary parameter slice; the proof identifies the boundary/rotation mechanism rather than reporting a simple numerical constant. No extension to higher order is claimed.
